chapterTitle: Understanding Arrays and Contiguous Dynamic Storage
title: Inspecting Adjacent Vector Element Addresses
adaptationNote: Display offsets in elements using pointer subtraction rather than implementation-specific integer addresses. The original byte-offset demonstration is preserved unchanged.

guide.problem: Store growing data in adjacent positions.
guide.design: A vector or owning array offers direct index access. A linked structure is useful for some insertions but loses adjacency.
guide.invariant: Logical size never exceeds capacity; live elements remain owned until removed or the container ends.
guide.failure: Keeping a pointer across reallocation can leave it dangling. Reading at size() is outside the live range.
guide.trace: Capacity doubling can progress 1,2,4,8 while logical sizes progress 1,2,3,4,5.
guide.maintenance: Separate logical bounds, storage allocation, and observer lifetime in reviews.
